nodes.name: Fighter core update loop
nodes.purpose: Coordinates controller sampling, status transitions, physics integration, hit processing, and match setup for every fighter.

nodes.name: Fighter attribute tables
nodes.purpose: Holds per-character movement, jump, air, weight, shield, and camera tuning values loaded from relocated data.

nodes.name: Fighter physics integrator
nodes.purpose: Applies gravity, terminal velocity, fast fall, air drift, surface friction, and ground-to-air velocity transfer on each update.

nodes.name: Ground movement states
nodes.purpose: Groups walk tiers, dash, run transitions, and ground speed limits shared by every fighter.

nodes.name: Jump and aerial states
nodes.purpose: Groups jump squat, short hop, double jump, fall, landing, platform drop, and tech windows.

nodes.name: Damage and hit reaction
nodes.purpose: Converts hit data into knockback, hitstun, damage levels, hitlag, and directional influence.

nodes.name: Shield and guard
nodes.purpose: Tracks shield health, decay, size scaling, shieldstun, and pushback for guarding fighters.

nodes.name: Ledge and blast zone
nodes.purpose: Implements ledge hold limits, re-grab timing, and out-of-bounds knockout checks.

nodes.name: Battle camera
nodes.purpose: Frames fighter targets, adjusts zoom and field of view, and smooths camera travel.

nodes.name: Map collision
nodes.purpose: Provides floor material friction, kinetic state changes, landing checks, and map line queries.

nodes.name: Attack collision sweep
nodes.purpose: Performs swept attack and hurtbox tests, joint-attached hitbox placement, and inverse-size scaling.

cards.name: Walk speed tiers
cards.summary: Stick tilt selects slow, medium, or fast walk, and ground speed follows stick displacement scaled by a per-fighter multiplier.
cards.behavior: The game compares absolute horizontal stick displacement with two thresholds to choose a walk tier, and it enters walk only after the stick crosses a small dead zone. Ground speed is driven toward stick displacement times the fighter walk multiplier, then reduced by the fighter traction value. Releasing the stick lets friction bring speed to zero without reversing direction.

cards.name: Dash and run transition
cards.summary: A quick stick flick starts a dash with a burst of speed, and holding the direction converts it to a run after a character-specific frame.
cards.behavior: Dash entry needs horizontal stick beyond a large threshold inside a short input window. Dash speed starts at the fighter dash value, begins losing speed after a fixed frame, and switches to run once the dash animation reaches the fighter dash-to-run frame while the stick stays held. Ending a dash without running leaves a fraction of the ground speed.

cards.name: Jump force and short hop
cards.summary: Jump height comes from stick force or button force, with the short-hop choice made inside a three-frame window.
cards.behavior: A grounded jump first enters a knee-bend state whose length comes from the fighter table. Stick jumps keep the largest vertical stick value seen during that state, while button jumps derive force from horizontal stick displacement and choose short or long force. The short-hop flag is latched only when a button releases within the first three frames, and the final vertical velocity is clamped before launch.

cards.name: Double jump and multi-jump
cards.summary: An airborne jump consumes one jump charge, applies a fighter-scaled vertical impulse, and lets a few fighters chain extra jumps.
cards.behavior: The aerial jump uses the full controller range as its force, multiplies it by the fighter jump height values and the aerial height factor, then increments the jump count. Horizontal aerial speed uses a separate per-fighter multiplier. Some fighters can reverse facing during the first twelve frames, and two character families have fixed declining velocities for their extra jumps.

cards.name: Fast fall
cards.summary: A downward stick flick while falling sets vertical speed to the fighter fast-fall terminal velocity and marks the landing as heavy.
cards.behavior: Fast fall arms only when the fighter is already descending and the stick crosses a deep downward threshold inside a short input window. Once armed, vertical speed is written directly to the fighter fast-fall terminal value on each update, ignoring normal gravity acceleration. Landing checks compare falling speed with that same terminal value to choose the heavy landing animation.

cards.name: Air drift and gravity
cards.summary: Air control adds acceleration from stick input, clamps horizontal speed, and applies friction when the stick is near neutral.
cards.behavior: Each update subtracts gravity from vertical speed and clamps descent at the fighter normal terminal velocity. Horizontal drift needs stick displacement above a small dead zone; stick input adds acceleration, the result is clamped to the fighter maximum air speed, and air friction pulls the value toward zero after drift is applied. When current horizontal speed already exceeds the maximum, the code steps it down toward the limit instead of clamping instantly.

cards.name: Ground friction by surface
cards.summary: Ground friction combines a floor material value with fighter traction, and knockback sliding uses a quarter of that friction.
cards.behavior: Ground speed loses friction each update until it reaches zero, and the amount is the floor material coefficient multiplied by the fighter traction attribute. A speed clamp on the opposite side prevents friction from reversing direction. While a fighter slides from damage on the ground, the same material and traction product is scaled down before it is applied.

cards.name: Knockback formula
cards.summary: Hit damage and accumulated percent feed a scaled knockback value that mixes fighter weight, attack scaling, and handicap.
cards.behavior: When a hit has no fixed knockback weight, the game adds current percent to queued damage, scales it by a damage coefficient and by hit damage, then multiplies by the defender weight factor. It adds a flat base, applies attack scale and base values, applies the match damage ratio, and multiplies both handicap table entries. The result is capped before it becomes launch speed.

cards.name: Hitstun and damage levels
cards.summary: Knockback becomes hitstun at a fixed divisor, and hitstun selects a light, medium, heavy, or airborne reaction.
cards.behavior: Hitstun is knockback divided by a constant, so launch speed and stun length stay proportional. The game compares the result with three thresholds to pick one of four reaction levels; the highest level lifts the fighter off the ground. A forced status override also promotes the reaction to the airborne level.

cards.name: Hitlag freeze
cards.summary: Each hit freezes both fighters for a damage-scaled number of updates, while button presses stay buffered.
cards.behavior: Hitlag length comes from damage divided by three plus a flat value, then is scaled by the hit multiplier; crouching cuts the result to two thirds. During hitlag the game skips physics and animation advances but records new button presses so they register when the freeze ends. Electric hits use a larger hitlag multiplier stored on the attacker.

cards.name: Smash directional influence
cards.summary: A fast stick flick during hitlag shifts the fighter position by stick displacement times a damage-direction multiplier.
cards.behavior: During hitlag, if stick magnitude reaches the smash threshold and either axis was tapped within the input buffer, the fighter model translates directly by the stick vector times the multiplier. The tap counters reset so one flick produces one shift. The multiplier differs between regions.

cards.name: Shield decay and size
cards.summary: Shield health drains on a fixed interval, regenerates slowly out of guard, and controls shield size.
cards.behavior: A guarding fighter loses one shield health every sixteen updates until the shield breaks. Outside guard, a shield below full heals one point every ten updates. Shield scale blends a health ratio with fixed scale constants and the fighter shield size attribute; a break resets health to a fixed low value.

cards.name: Shieldstun and pushback
cards.summary: Blocked damage becomes shieldstun frames, and those frames drive horizontal pushback on the defender.
cards.behavior: When a hit is blocked, shield damage is multiplied by a regional constant and a flat bonus is added to produce shieldstun frames. The defender slides away from the attacker at a speed equal to those frames times a velocity multiplier, while the release delay still counts down.

cards.name: Ledge hold and re-grab
cards.summary: Ledge hold time shortens with damage, and a cooldown blocks immediate re-grabs.
cards.behavior: After grabbing a ledge, a fighter waits a long fixed time at low damage and a shorter time at high damage. When the wait expires, the fighter drops away and starts a ledge catch cooldown.

cards.name: Platform drop-through
cards.summary: A deep downward stick flick drops a fighter through a passable platform by ignoring the current floor line.
cards.behavior: The drop check needs the stick below a downward threshold within a short tap window and a floor flagged as passable. Entering the state clears vertical speed, clamps horizontal air speed, and ignores the floor line just left. Crouch can queue the same drop for a few frames.

cards.name: Tech window
cards.summary: A Z press shortly before impact converts a knockdown into a tech, and a missed tech allows a directional roll.
cards.behavior: The game tracks updates since the last Z press and treats a press inside a twenty-frame window as a tech request when a damage collision is about to ground the fighter. A failed tech can still become a directional get-up roll when horizontal stick passes a small threshold.

cards.name: Battle camera framing
cards.summary: The battle camera frames all fighters inside facing-biased boxes, zooms with player count, and smooths field of view and travel.
cards.behavior: Each fighter contributes a box that reaches farther in front than behind based on facing, plus a fixed vertical margin. The union sets horizontal and vertical interest, which becomes a target distance clamped between fixed limits. Player count picks a zoom multiplier, and camera travel and field of view move toward their targets by a fraction each update.

cards.name: Blast zone knockout
cards.summary: Crossing a stage map boundary knocks a fighter out, with a random upward star knockout at the top boundary.
cards.behavior: Each update compares the fighter top joint against map bounds, ignoring bosses and fighters flagged to stay inside. A bottom or side crossing starts a directional knockout; a top crossing picks a star launch most of the time and the upward fall launch otherwise. In limit mode the same bounds teleport the fighter inward instead of causing a knockout.

constants.name: top upward-fall knockout chance denominator
constants.unit: one in N top-boundary knockouts at 60 Hz

constants.name: limit mode inward offset
constants.unit: world units, applied each 60 Hz update

cards.name: Swept hitbox placement
cards.summary: Attack colliders follow animated joints and sweep from their previous position to their current position for hit tests.
cards.behavior: On the first active update an attack collider copies its offset and converts it to world space from its joint. Later updates keep the previous position, recompute the current position, and hit tests sweep the segment between them. Collider offsets can be scaled by the inverse of the fighter size attribute so the same animation works at different body scales.

constants.unit: size multiplier, applied per hitbox update at 60 Hz

constants.name: inverse size numerator
constants.unit: size ratio numerator, applied per hitbox update at 60 Hz
